name: Boswellia serrata extract

It is commercially valued for its boswellic acid content, which drives demand across nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic supply chains. In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is formulated into capsules, tablets, and softgels targeting joint and mobility support categories. This represents one of the highest-volume botanical supplement segments globally for industrial buyers. These applications require consistent solubility and potency for large-scale production. Cosmetic formulators use it in anti-aging creams and serums, where boswellic acid content supports claims around skin conditioning and oxidative stress protection. It is a key ingredient for high-end personal care product lines. Pharmaceutical-grade extracts are also evaluated in topical and oral dosage forms requiring documented boswellic acid standardization. These materials must adhere to rigorous quality control protocols to ensure safety and efficacy. Boswellia serrata extract is supplied as a fine powder, typically standardized to defined boswellic acid concentrations. Premium supplement grades are commonly standardized to 65% or higher to meet industry benchmarks. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are available, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting stricter purity and heavy metal limits. This ensures compliance with international safety regulations and manufacturing requirements.
